main_text.p: & Thomam Urothum, equites ornatissimos: aliosque complures, non minus comitatem & mansuetudinem animi tui, quàm familiæ splendorem & amplitudinem prædicare: ut mihi facile persuadeā, non ingratam Celsitudini tuæ hanc qualemcunq; animi erga illam mei significationem fore. Vir amplissime & Comes illustrissime, Vale, & salue. Deus Opt. Max. Celsitudinem tuam diu nobis incolumem conseruet, cuius me fidei & clientelæ demississimè & studiosissimè commendo. Argentorati, x Cal. Feb.

page.notes: Two small ornaments (asterisk-like marks) below the text and a few specks on the page were not transcribed; they are not printed words. The first word of the page is written "Urothum" for the printed "Vurothum", following the u/v rule. "amplitudinem" is split across a line end in the scan with no clearly visible hyphen; it is written whole. The date line is copied as printed, with spaces and stops.
